system.name: TxCheck
system.one_liner: an approach that detects transactional bugs in DBMS engines by constructing statement-dependency graphs and comparing semantically equivalent schedules

content.key_idea: Colour links two overlapping instrumented-read outputs, (1,20) and (2,43,8), directly to the predicate-anti and item-anti edges they produce in the inferred statement-dependency graph.
content.reading_order: top-down through the instrumented test case's statements, following the blue and red highlighted lines down their dashed connectors into the matching coloured edges of the dependency graph below

palette.used_for: blue highlight on the BWR/VSR0 code-line boxes and the 'predicate-anti' edge, marking the (1,20) overlap
red highlight on the T0.S2/T1.S3.BWR code-line boxes and the 'item-anti' edge (T0.S2→T1.S3), marking the (2,43,8) overlap
white fill of the dependency-graph node boxes (T1.S1, T1.S2, T1.S3, T0.S1, T0.S2)

style.stroke: thin black box outlines and graph edges; dashed blue/red connector lines from code to graph
style.arrows: thin black arrows for the dependency-graph edges, each labelled by dependency type

encoding.color_means: blue marks one pair of instrumented reads and the graph edge their overlap produces (predicate-anti); red marks a second such pair and edge (item-anti)
encoding.line_style_means: dashed connector lines carry a highlight colour from a specific code line down to the matching graph edge; the graph's own edges are solid
encoding.state_means: not applicable; a single static explanatory frame, not before/after or alternatives
encoding.marker_means: no numbered markers; box outlines and edge-label colour do the work of pointing out which lines produced which edge
encoding.emphasis: colour-matching a code-line box to a graph edge (rather than merely labelling the edge) lets the reader verify the dependency rule by eye, using concrete overlapping values
reusable_patterns: a code listing stacked above the graph it produces, with colour-coded dashed connectors tying specific highlighted lines to the specific edges they justify
weaknesses: with many near-identical SQL lines above, spotting which two are colour-boxed (versus merely italicised as commentary) takes a careful look

evidence: Figure 6 shows how the inserted statements are used to infer statement dependencies for the test case in Figure 1.
The output of T0.S2 and the output of BWR of T1.S3 have an overlapping part (i.e., item (2, 43, 8))
Therefore, T0.S2 is (stmt-item-anti) depended on T1.S3.

summary: This figure from TxCheck's approach section shows how statement dependencies are inferred for the Figure 1 test case using inserted BWR/AWR/VSR instrumentation statements. The top box lists the fully instrumented SQL log; two pairs of lines are highlighted where their outputs overlap: T0.S1.BWR and T1.S3.VSR0 both return item (1,20), shown in blue, while T0.S2 and T1.S3.BWR both return item (2,43,8), shown in red. Dashed connectors carry each highlighted colour down into the statement-dependency graph below, where the matching blue pair produces the predicate-anti edge from T1.S2/T1.S3 to T0.S1, and the matching red pair produces the item-anti edge from T0.S2 to T1.S3. The figure demonstrates, with concrete overlapping values, exactly how TxCheck's inference procedure turns instrumented-statement outputs into typed dependency edges.
summary_zh: 该图展示TxCheck如何利用BWR/AWR/VSR插桩语句为图1的测试用例推断语句依赖关系：T0.S1.BWR与T1.S3.VSR0均读到重叠值(1,20)(蓝色高亮)，对应下方依赖图中的predicate-anti边；T0.S2与T1.S3.BWR均读到重叠值(2,43,8)(红色高亮)，对应item-anti边，用具体数值演示了依赖推断的完整过程。
notes: Corrected content.base from prior 'code' to 'mixed': the figure equally emphasises a code listing (the instrumented test case) and a node-link graph (the statement-dependency graph), joined by colour-coded cross-representation mapping lines, rather than being purely a code artifact. Kept worked_example as prior False since the concrete (1,20)/(2,43,8) values here illustrate a general dependency-inference mechanism (the teaching point survives if different example numbers were substituted), unlike Figure 1/14's row-count-is-the-point framing in the same paper.
